detailed_rationale:
Anant Raj is a Delhi-NCR-focused real estate developer with a diversified portfolio -- residential townships, group housing, IT parks, hotels, commercial complexes, malls, service apartments and warehousing (11.3 million sq ft developed to date) -- that has been pivoting meaningfully into data centers, currently operating about 28 MW of data-center capacity. FY26 (year to Mar 2026) revenue grew about 22% to roughly Rs 2,512 crore (matching the quant screen's revenue_growth_1y of 21.88%), with net profit of about Rs 559 crore (EPS Rs 15.42) and a healthy 26% operating margin. Returns on capital are meaningfully better on current data than the quant screen reflects: ROE is about 11.2% (last year) and ROCE about 12.1% on the latest available data, versus the quant screen's much staler 4.7%/4.9% -- a large enough gap that the better, more current figures should be used. The balance sheet has genuinely de-levered over time: borrowings fell from about Rs 1,721 crore (Mar 2017) to about Rs 681 crore (Mar 2026), consistent with the quant screen's low D/E of 0.12x and very high interest coverage of 54.7x. Working capital days are high (346 days as of Mar 2026), but this is a normal feature of real estate development (long land-acquisition-to-sale cycles) rather than a company-specific red flag. Promoter holding has declined 5.80 percentage points over three years to about 57.43% -- a moderate trend, not extreme.

The single most important recent development is corporate-structural, not operating: the company's board has approved a demerger plan (approved July 21, 2026) under which ARCPL will first be merged into Anant Raj, and the data-center business will then be separated into a new entity (ACPL) for a standalone listing. This is a major restructuring that will directly change what current shareholders hold -- effectively splitting a blended real-estate-plus-data-center company into two separately listed pieces -- and the quant screen's trailing, consolidated financial ratios (which blend a modest-ROE, high-working-capital-days real estate business with a much faster-growing, presumably higher-multiple data-center business) cannot reflect how the market will value the pieces separately once the demerger completes. Sum-of-the-parts logic (a growing hyperscaler-driven data-center pure-play, spun out at scale, alongside a legacy Delhi-NCR realty business) could plausibly unlock value that the current single PE multiple (about 40.5x) does not clearly convey either way.
recommendation_rationale: The quant screen carries this as Hold, with middling quality and value scores reflecting a blended real-estate-plus-data-center business that is hard to value cleanly as a single entity. My own view agrees with Hold as the standing recommendation, but I am escalating because the approved demerger (splitting the data-center business into a separately listed entity) is a specific, dated, board-approved corporate action that will materially change the investment case and that a static quant screen on consolidated financials cannot capture -- this is exactly the kind of structural event the escalation channel is meant to surface, not a routine valuation judgment call. I am not converting this to Sell (there's a credible bull case in the data-center carve-out), simply flagging that this position needs active tracking through the demerger process rather than a routine, passive Hold treatment.
summary: Anant Raj is a Delhi-NCR real estate developer that has been building a meaningful data-center business (28 MW of capacity so far) alongside its traditional residential, commercial and hospitality projects. The company has approved a plan to separate the data-center business into its own separately listed company, which will change what current shareholders hold. The underlying business has grown well recently and the balance sheet has improved significantly over time. We rate it a Hold, but flag that the pending demerger is a major structural event investors should track closely rather than assume away.
positive_para: A genuinely improving balance sheet (borrowings down from about Rs 1,721 crore in FY17 to about Rs 681 crore in FY26), solid recent growth (revenue +22%, healthy 26% operating margin), and a real, scaling data-center business (28 MW) riding India's structural cloud/AI-driven data-center demand growth, now set to be separately listed via a board-approved demerger that could let the market value each piece of the business on its own merits.
negative_para: Returns on capital remain modest for a real-estate-plus-infrastructure business (ROE about 11.2%) even after using the more current figures, working capital days are high (346, typical for the sector but still a real cash-conversion drag), and -- most importantly -- the pending demerger creates real near-term uncertainty about execution, timing and how the two resulting entities will be valued, which the current 40.5x trailing PE on the blended business does not cleanly resolve either way.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At about 40.5x trailing earnings on a blended real-estate-and-data-center business, the multiple likely already gives credit for the data-center growth story, but it is genuinely difficult to assess whether that credit is well-calibrated until the demerger completes and the market can price the data-center entity (ACPL) and the legacy realty business separately -- this is a name where sum-of-the-parts logic matters more than a single blended multiple. Growth here is estimated below the 25% hypergrowth band given the real uncertainty around demerger execution and timing, so the ROE/dilution disclosure is not separately triggered, though continued data-center capex will likely require ongoing capital allocation decisions worth watching post-demerger.
escalation_reason: The board has approved a demerger (approved July 21, 2026) that will merge ARCPL into Anant Raj and then separate the data-center business (28 MW capacity) into a new standalone-listed entity (ACPL). This is a specific, dated, major corporate-structural action that will change what current shareholders hold and how the business should be valued (sum-of-parts vs. today's single blended multiple) -- something the quant screen's trailing consolidated financials cannot capture. Worth portfolio-manager attention on how to treat this position through the demerger (e.g., whether to hold through the split, and how to value each resulting entity), independent of today's routine Hold call.
technical_commentary: Anant Raj ran hard into a Jan-2025 ATH (Rs934) then broke down sharply, and 2026's yearly high so far (Rs591) is a much lower high, well below 2025's peak -- a real structural break. The monthly MA stack is jumbled (price above the 40-month average but the 10-month sits below the 20-month, a rolling-over signature) even as the stock attempts to stabilize (+14% over 6 months); this reads as an unproven repair attempt after a genuine top, not a resumed uptrend yet.
